articles.title: Safety and Clinical Impact of Emergency Department Closed Reduction for Gartland Type III Supracondylar Humerus Fractures.
articles.authors: Kelley NH, Carroll CJ, Shaver T, Newcomb NL, Marasigan JAM
articles.population: Children with extension-type 3 supracondylar humerus fractures
articles.sample_size: 112 patients (54 underwent closed reduction, 58 did not)
articles.outcomes: Neurovascular examination findings, radiographic alignment parameters, time to operating room, operative time, and vascular injury rates
articles.take_home: Emergency department closed reduction of severe supracondylar humerus fractures in children is safe and improved vascular function and fracture alignment in this study. Children who did not receive early reduction were more likely to develop nerve problems whilst waiting for surgery.

articles.title: The Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0 : structural validity and responsiveness as a patient-centred tool for assessing recovery after medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction.
articles.authors: Sze IN, Kerslake S, Hiemstra LA
articles.study_type: Validation study of a patient-reported outcome measure
articles.population: Patients undergoing medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: BPII 2.0 structural validity, internal consistency, construct validity, and responsiveness at 6, 12, and 24 months post-surgery across five domains: recreation, lifestyle, social/emotional wellbeing, work/school concerns, and symptoms
articles.take_home: The BPII 2.0 questionnaire is a reliable and valid tool for measuring how well patients recover after kneecap ligament surgery, with most improvement happening in the first six months and stabilising by 12 months, though social and recreational activities tend to recover more slowly.

articles.title: Semaglutide for the Treatment of Obesity in Children 6 to <12 Years of Age.
articles.authors: Jastreboff AM, Harder-Lauridsen NM, Van Name M, Korner A, Kelly AS, Weghuber D, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 6 to under 12 years with obesity
articles.outcomes: Percent change in BMI at 68 weeks was -13.5% with semaglutide versus 2.7% with placebo. At 68 weeks, 79% of semaglutide group had reduction in BMI category compared to 23% of placebo group. 38% of semaglutide group had BMI below obesity threshold versus 2% of placebo group. Gastrointestinal adverse events were more common with semaglutide.
articles.take_home: Semaglutide injection once a week reduced BMI significantly more than placebo in children aged 6 to 12 with obesity over 68 weeks, with more than three-quarters of treated children showing improvement in their weight category. The main side effects were stomach-related problems, which were more common with semaglutide but usually mild.

articles.title: Osteoarticular Infection in Immunocompromised Children and Neonates: A Retrospective Case Series Emphasising Diagnostic Challenges and Multimodal Management.
articles.authors: Mishra N, Lee NKL, Tan NWH, Chong CY, Seow CWX, Zainuddin MAB, et al.
articles.population: Neonates and immunocompromised children under 16 years with bone or joint infections
articles.outcomes: 77.8% had complete resolution; 2 died from unrelated causes; 1 lost to follow-up; 1 had persistent or recurrent infection; 2 developed chronic musculoskeletal complications
articles.take_home: Bone and joint infections in immunocompromised children and neonates can be difficult to spot because fever and high white blood cell counts may not appear, but CRP blood markers are usually raised. Most children improved well with a combination of surgery and antibiotics, though some had long-term problems.

articles.title: Locking-compression plate (LCP) or angled blade plates (ABP) for femoral osteotomies in children with spastic cerebral palsy (CP) gross motor function classification system (GMFCS) III, IV, and V.
articles.authors: Zaldivar B, Ramirez-Schneider LC, Balcazar-Munoz EI, Arango-Piedrahita N, Macallister-Diaz JN, Mafla-Gomez M, et al.
articles.population: Children under 18 years with spastic cerebral palsy GMFCS III-V undergoing femoral osteotomies
articles.outcomes: Hardware-related complications (implant failure, peri-implant fracture, non-union), operative time, and blood loss
articles.take_home: Locking-compression plates and angled blade plates had similar overall complication rates for femoral osteotomies in children with severe cerebral palsy. Locking-compression plates took longer to place and caused more blood loss, whilst angled blade plates showed more problems at the lower thigh bone.

articles.title: Improving Surveillance Duration for Developmental Dysplasia of the Hip: A Single-Center Retrospective Quality Improvement Initiative.
articles.authors: Bozzo I, Gagnon M, Legler J, Tangadulrat P, Benaroch T
articles.population: Infants with risk factors for developmental dysplasia of the hip (first-degree relative with DDH or breech gestation) who had normal ultrasound screening
articles.sample_size: 4233 patients referred for screening; 2497 returned for follow-up radiograph
articles.outcomes: Prevalence of developmental dysplasia of the hip requiring surgical intervention (closed or open reduction or other surgery)
articles.take_home: None of the 4233 high-risk infants with normal initial hip ultrasound developed dysplasia needing treatment during follow-up. This suggests that routine follow-up X-rays may not be necessary and could be reduced to avoid unnecessary radiation and hospital visits.

articles.title: Clinical and radiological outcomes of open reduction and internal fixation for Kilfoyle type III pediatric medial humeral condyle fractures: a retrospective single-center study.
articles.authors: Maleki A, Pirasteh MN, Salajegheh A
articles.population: Children aged 18 months to 12 years with displaced medial humeral condyle fractures
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union, elbow range of motion, complications including nonunion, malunion, cubitus varus, and extension deficit
articles.take_home: Open reduction and internal fixation successfully healed the fracture in 94% of children, with most regaining good elbow movement. However, about one third of patients developed complications such as altered elbow alignment or reduced extension, particularly in older children.

articles.title: Preventing Malaria Infections and Moving toward Malaria Elimination.
articles.authors: Tchouatieu AM, Wells TNC, Achan J
articles.population: People at risk of malaria, predominantly African children
articles.outcomes: Current and emerging approaches to malaria prevention including vector control, chemoprevention, monoclonal antibodies and vaccines
articles.take_home: Malaria prevention is being transformed by new tools like long-acting injectable treatments and improved vaccines, but success will depend on countries combining these interventions in ways that suit their own populations and strengthening their surveillance and healthcare systems.

articles.title: Development and Validation of a Patient and Caregiver Expectations Survey for Posterior Spinal Fusion for Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis.
articles.authors: Kiani SN, Cazzulino A, Niknam K, Coufal S, Katyal T, Swarup I
articles.population: Adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal fusion and their guardians
articles.sample_size: 30 patient-guardian pairs (15 for development, 15 for validation)
articles.outcomes: Development of two 10-item Likert-scale expectation surveys (one for patients, one for guardians); validation through test-retest reliability using Cohen kappa statistics
articles.take_home: Researchers created surveys to measure what adolescents and their guardians expect before scoliosis surgery, with the surveys showing good reliability. However, adolescents and their guardians often have different expectations about surgery outcomes, so these surveys may help surgeons better prepare families for what to expect.

articles.title: Arthrofibrosis After Pediatric ACL Reconstruction: Associated Factors and Role of Graft Type, a Retrospective Study.
articles.authors: Thai S, Rauf R, Le Y, Elsabbagh Z, ElNemer W, Park K, et al.
articles.population: Paediatric patients undergoing primary ACL reconstruction with hamstring or quadriceps tendon autograft
articles.sample_size: 154 patients (84 hamstring tendon, 70 quadriceps tendon); mean age 15.1 years
articles.outcomes: Arthrofibrosis development (defined as loss of 10 degrees or more extension, 20 degrees or more flexion, or mechanical symptoms); knee range of motion; need for additional surgery
articles.take_home: Quadriceps tendon grafts were associated with a higher rate of arthrofibrosis (stiffness) and loss of knee motion compared to hamstring tendon grafts in young patients. Graft choice may need to be tailored based on individual patient factors such as associated cartilage damage.

articles.title: A blended digital parenting intervention for the prevention of sexual violence, exploitative sex, and maltreatment of children at scale in Tanzania: a cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
articles.authors: Cluver LD, Ornellas A, Klapwijk JM, Nyalali K, Chetty AN, Mgunga S, et al.
articles.population: Primary caregivers aged 18 years and older and their adolescents aged 10-17 years in Tanzania
articles.outcomes: Adolescent sexual violence victimisation, maltreatment (physical abuse, verbal abuse, neglect), and exposure to high-risk situations for sexual violence at 5 and 18 months
articles.take_home: A low-cost digital parenting app delivered on Android phones significantly reduced sexual violence against girls and reduced maltreatment and high-risk situations for both girls and boys. The intervention cost only £6 per family at scale and worked without needing to mask participants or researchers.

articles.title: Tibiofibular Relationships in Children With Achondroplasia: A Comparative Radiographic Study.
articles.authors: Rovira Marti MP, Garcia Fontecha CG, Torner Rubies F
articles.population: Children under 21 years with achondroplasia and control children without conditions affecting lower-limb alignment
articles.sample_size: 121 children (63 with achondroplasia, 58 controls) contributing 239 radiographic examinations
articles.outcomes: Tibiofibular relationships measured by fibular extension, fibula-to-tibia length ratio, and their associations with mechanical axis deviation and tibial alignment angles
articles.take_home: Children with achondroplasia have relative fibular overgrowth compared to other children, and the degree of this overgrowth is associated with the development of inward-angled leg deformities. These findings may help guide surgical planning for tibial lengthening procedures.

articles.title: Demographic Characteristics and Complications of ORIF in Pediatric Tibial Tubercle Fractures.
articles.authors: Abid R, Jayakumar PL, Burkhart RJ, Adelstein JM, Hardesty CK, Liu RW, et al.
articles.study_type: Population-based cohort study using electronic health records
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 17 years or younger treated with open reduction and internal fixation for tibial tubercle fractures
articles.outcomes: Postoperative complications including compartment syndrome, surgical site infection, and osteomyelitis at 30-day, 90-day, 180-day, and 2-year follow-up; rates of revision surgery and implant removal; prevalence of pre-existing Osgood-Schlatter disease
articles.take_home: Open reduction and internal fixation for tibial tubercle fractures in children is safe, with serious complications like infection occurring in less than 1.5% of cases. However, about 5% of patients needed repeat surgery within 30 days, and 13% had their metal implants removed by 2 years.
